passage.bullet: Bismarck’s 1862 Blood and Iron speech prioritised armed force over parliamentary debate → drove unification

Prussia outgunned Denmark and rival Austria → secured unchallenged dominance across Northern Germany

stems.stem: Rejecting peaceful debate in 1862, ____________ argued that ____________ alone would unite the fragmented German states.

lesson_1.watch_out: Prussia was the leading northern German kingdom that unified Germany—do not confuse Prussia with Tsarist Russia.

passage.bullet: Bismarck provoked war with France in July 1870 → rallied independent southern German states together
Prussian forces trapped Emperor Napoleon III and 80,000 French troops at Sedan → toppled regime

context.bullet: Unified Germany replaced France as mainland Europe’s leading industrial and military superpower

stems.stem: By provoking conflict with France in July 1870, Bismarck persuaded ____________ to join Prussia.
Trapping ____________ alongside ____________ soldiers at Sedan shattered France’s imperial government.
On 18 January 1871, German princes proclaimed ____________ inside Versailles, transforming Europe’s power balance.

lesson_1.watch_out: Kaiser Wilhelm I was crowned inside France’s Palace of Versailles in 1871—not in Berlin, making French humiliation deliberate.

passage.bullet: France had to pay 5 billion gold francs → crippled French state finances after defeat
German troops occupied French cities until full payment → served as a daily national humiliation
Germany seized coal- and iron-rich Alsace-Lorraine → stripped France of vital border land and industry

context.bullet: Punitive Frankfurt terms poisoned Franco-German diplomacy for forty years → blocked peaceful reconciliation
Control of Metz and frontier passes → pushed German armies closer to the French heartland

stems.stem: Under the punitive 1871 settlement, German occupation soldiers stayed in French cities until ____________ was paid.
Annexing the border provinces of ____________ cost France valuable ____________ reserves alongside loyal citizens.
Rather than securing lasting peace, these harsh terms poisoned ____________ for the next four decades.

lesson_1.watch_out: Do not confuse the 1871 Treaty of Frankfurt with the 1919 Treaty of Versailles—Frankfurt punished France after 1870.

passage.bullet: Primary teachers draped Alsace-Lorraine in black crepe on wall maps → kept loss visible daily
French pupils were taught to mourn lost provinces → raised a generation hungry for revenge
Universal conscription at age twenty → trained millions of young Frenchmen for future continental war

context.bullet: Anger over the 1871 Treaty of Frankfurt → turned reclaiming Alsace-Lorraine into a sacred duty

stems.stem: Every morning in French primary schools, maps of the eastern border were veiled in ____________ to mourn lost land.
Growing up under the cult of revanche, pupils viewed liberating ____________ as their patriotic duty.
Enforcing universal ____________ for men aged ____________ built a vast reserve trained for continental war.

lesson_1.watch_out: Revanche means national vengeance and recovery of lost territory—do not confuse it with internal political revolution.

passage.bullet: Bismarck dreaded a two-front war against France in the west and Russia in the east
The secret 1887 Reinsurance Treaty with Tsarist Russia → pledged mutual neutrality in major wars
Keeping St Petersburg tied to Berlin → denied vengeful France any powerful continental ally

context.bullet: Bismarck already held the 1879 Dual Alliance with Austria-Hungary → balanced rival eastern empires carefully
Dropping this Russian treaty after Bismarck’s 1890 dismissal → drove Russia straight into French arms

stems.stem: Haunted by the prospect of fighting on ____________ simultaneously, Bismarck prioritised cautious continental diplomacy.
Negotiating the secret 1887 ____________ secured Russian ____________ if France attacked Germany.
Preventing a Franco-Russian partnership kept ____________ isolated and unable to wage a war of revanche.

lesson_1.watch_out: The 1887 Reinsurance Treaty promised neutrality rather than joint invasion—Bismarck wanted peace to protect Germany’s 1871 gains.

passage.bullet: Industrial powers craved rubber, copper, palm oil, and cotton → fuelled fierce competition in Africa
Bismarck hosted the 1884 Berlin Conference → set agreed rules to stop rival Europeans clashing
Demanding proof of effective occupation on the ground → triggered a rapid race inland

context.bullet: Zero African rulers were invited to Berlin → arbitrary colonial borders carved through existing kingdoms
Bismarck encouraged French colonial expansion overseas → distracted Paris from mourning lost Alsace-Lorraine

stems.stem: Hungry for industrial raw materials such as ____________, European powers raced to claim African territory.
Hosting the 1884 ____________ allowed Bismarck to regulate colonial claims before rival empires fought.
Insisting on proof of ____________ forced European armies to march rapidly into the African interior.

lesson_2.watch_out: Bismarck hosted the 1884 Berlin Conference to prevent European colonial wars—not to grab the largest empire for Germany.

passage.bullet: Young Kaiser Wilhelm II dismissed Bismarck in 1890 → scrapped cautious European balance-of-power diplomacy
Wilhelm envied vast British and French empires → demanded Germany’s own place in the sun
Pursuing Weltpolitik across Africa and Asia → required colonies and a fleet rivalling Britain

context.bullet: Wilhelm let the 1887 Reinsurance Treaty expire in 1890 → freed Russia to ally with France
Surging German steel and coal output after 1871 → emboldened Berlin to demand world-power status

stems.stem: Dismissing cautious veteran ____________ in 1890, twenty-nine-year-old Wilhelm II steered Germany toward aggressive global expansion.
Envious of British and French territories, Berlin demanded ____________ through its assertive new ____________ strategy.
Acquiring distant colonies across Africa and the Pacific meant building ____________ that alarmed Great Britain.

lesson_2.watch_out: Bismarck wanted to keep Germany safe inside Europe, whereas Wilhelm II’s Weltpolitik chased overseas colonies and naval prestige.

passage.bullet: Wilhelm paraded through Tangier backing Moroccan independence → directly challenged French control in North Africa
Berlin probed the 1904 Entente Cordiale → tested whether Britain would truly defend French interests

context.bullet: Under the 1904 Entente Cordiale, Britain backed France in Morocco in return for Egypt
France’s ally Russia was reeling from defeat against Japan in 1905 → emboldened Wilhelm’s gamble

stems.stem: Landing unannounced in March 1905, Wilhelm declared support for ____________ to block French expansion.
Berlin staged this North African crisis to see if ____________ would stand by the 1904 ____________.
Forcing France to back down was meant to humiliate Paris and split ____________ apart.

lesson_2.watch_out: Wilhelm II did not care genuinely about Moroccan freedom—he used Tangier as a diplomatic wedge against the Entente Cordiale.

passage.bullet: Twelve nations outvoted Germany at Algeciras, leaving only Austria-Hungary loyal → exposed Berlin’s diplomatic isolation

context.bullet: Even Triple Alliance partner Italy voted against Berlin at Algeciras → exposed cracks in Germany’s bloc

stems.stem: Outvoted by ____________ at the Spanish summit, Germany found itself backed only by ____________.

Wilhelm’s Tangier gamble backfired by cementing Anglo-French ties and deepening German dread of ____________.

lesson_2.watch_out: The 1904 Entente Cordiale was originally a colonial friendship—German bullying at Algeciras turned it into secret military planning.

passage.bullet: Anchoring SMS Panther at Agadir → sparked British fears of a German Atlantic naval base

context.bullet: A German port on Morocco’s Atlantic coast → threatened vital British food and imperial trade routes

stems.stem: Anchoring the warship ____________ at Agadir convinced Whitehall that Berlin wanted ____________ on the Atlantic.

lesson_2.watch_out: Do not mix up the two Moroccan crises—Tangier in 1905 involved the Kaiser’s visit, whereas Agadir in 1911 involved SMS Panther.

passage.bullet: Ships carried over sixty percent of Britain’s food → enemy blockade meant rapid civilian starvation
Parliament’s 1889 law required outmatching French and Russian fleets combined → locked in maritime supremacy

stems.stem: Importing over ____________ of its food by sea meant an enemy blockade would starve British civilians.

lesson_3.watch_out: In 1889 the Two-Power Standard targeted France and Russia—Germany had not yet begun building its High Seas Fleet.

lesson_3.watch_out: Tirpitz’s Risk Theory did not need a fleet larger than Britain’s—only one strong enough to cripple Royal Navy global dominance.
